title: The Marine Corps’ Plan for the Future of Ground Combat
gist: A War on the Rocks podcast previews the U.S. Marine Corps' newly released ground-warfare plan, Ground Combat Element 2040, discussed with its two architects. The conversation centers on drones, resilience, long-range fires, and logistics for surviving an increasingly transparent battlefield while preserving the human element.

insights.claim: The U.S. Marine Corps has released a plan called Ground Combat Element 2040 for how it intends to fight adversaries on land in the future.
insights.speaker: Jason Morris, Erick Clark, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: A named service-level modernization plan signals near-term Marine Corps procurement priorities toward drones, fires, and logistics enablers.
insights.quote: The Marine Corps just released its plan to fight against adversaries on land
insights.locator: The Marine Corps just released its plan

insights.claim: The Marine Corps' future ground-combat plan foregrounds drones, resilience, long-range fires, and logistics as the capabilities marines will need to survive and fight.
insights.speaker: Jason Morris, Erick Clark, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: Points investors toward suppliers of unmanned systems, long-range fires, and contested logistics as Marine Corps demand areas.
insights.quote: They discuss drones, resilience, long-range fires, logistics, and what marines will need to survive and fight

insights.claim: Marine Corps planners frame the future ground battlefield as increasingly transparent, requiring new approaches to survivability while still preserving the critical human element.
insights.speaker: Jason Morris, Erick Clark, and Ryan Evans
insights.so_what: A 'transparent battlefield' framing implies durable demand for concealment, dispersion, counter-ISR, and autonomy technologies.
